title: Environmental Engineering Technologists and Technicians
description: Apply theory and principles of environmental engineering to modify, test, and operate equipment and devices used in the prevention, control, and remediation of environmental problems, including waste treatment and site remediation, under the direction of engineering staff or scientists. May assist in the development of environmental remediation devices.

tasks.text: Perform environmental quality work in field or office settings.
Maintain process parameters and evaluate process anomalies.
Assess the ability of environments to naturally remove or reduce conventional or emerging contaminants from air, water, or soil.
Work with customers to assess the environmental impact of proposed construction or to develop pollution prevention programs.
Improve chemical processes to reduce toxic emissions.
Maintain project logbook records or computer program files.
Record laboratory or field data, including numerical data, test results, photographs, or summaries of visual observations.
Produce environmental assessment reports, tabulating data and preparing charts, graphs, or sketches.
Decontaminate or test field equipment used to clean or test pollutants from soil, air, or water.
Inspect facilities to monitor compliance with regulations governing substances, such as asbestos, lead, or wastewater.
Receive, set up, test, or decontaminate equipment.
Collect and analyze pollution samples, such as air or ground water.
Review technical documents to ensure completeness and conformance to requirements.
Perform statistical analysis and correction of air or water pollution data submitted by industry or other agencies.
Assist in the cleanup of hazardous material spills.
Arrange for the disposal of lead, asbestos, or other hazardous materials.

clusters.label: Drafting, Laying Out, and Specifying Technical Devices, Parts, and Equipment

tasks.text: Model biological, chemical, or physical treatment processes to remove or degrade pollutants.
Create models to demonstrate or predict the process by which pollutants move through or impact an environment.
Prepare and package environmental samples for shipping or testing.
Develop work plans, including writing specifications or establishing material, manpower, or facilities needs.
Evaluate and select technologies to clean up polluted sites, restore polluted air, water, or soil, or rehabilitate degraded ecosystems.
Provide technical engineering support in the planning of projects, such as wastewater treatment plants, to ensure compliance with environmental regulations and policies.
Prepare permit applications or review compliance with environmental permits.
Review work plans to schedule activities.
Oversee support staff.
Obtain product information, identify vendors or suppliers, or order materials or equipment to maintain inventory.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Science
skills.def: Using scientific rules and methods to solve problems.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Quality Control Analysis
skills.def: Conducting tests and inspections of products, services, or processes to evaluate quality or performance.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Mathematics
skills.def: Using mathematics to solve problems.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Operations Monitoring
skills.def: Watching gauges, dials, or other indicators to make sure a machine is working properly.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Management of Personnel Resources
skills.def: Motivating, developing, and directing people as they work, identifying the best people for the job.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Computer aided design CAD software
skills.def: Software to design 2D or 3D objects. May include engineering or architectural features. Examples: Autodesk AutoCAD, Autodesk AutoCAD Civil 3D, Bentley MicroStation, Computer aided design and drafting CADD software.

skills.name: Analytical or scientific software
skills.def: Software to capture data, perform analysis, or generate reports or visualizations to support scientific research. Examples: Air dispersion modeling software, ANSYS simulation software, DHI Water and Environment MIKE SHE, Ecological risk assessment software.

skills.name: Object or component oriented development software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications using object-oriented programming concepts. Examples: C++, Python.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Database software, Microsoft Access, Structure query language SQL.

skills.name: Geographic information system
skills.def: Software to capture, manage, analyze, or display geographically-referenced information. Examples: ESRI ArcGIS software, Geographic information system GIS software, Geographic information system GIS systems.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: Email software, Microsoft Outlook.
